questions.questionText: A firm uses a variety of strategies to improve its market position. Which one of the following strategies is most likely to benefit consumers in the long run?
options: An advertising campaign that promotes the product’s image
Charging low prices to drive rival firms out of the market
Investing in research and development to improve product quality
Merging with a rival to reduce competition in the market

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the production possibility boundary for petrol-powered cars and electric-powered cars in a country's car industry. If production has moved from Point A to Point B, which one of the following must be true?
options: Allocative efficiency in the car industry is unchanged
Demand for electric-powered vehicles has increased
Productive efficiency in the car industry is unchanged
Static efficiency in the car industry has improved

questions.questionText: A firm has a downward-sloping average revenue curve and a U-shaped average total cost curve. Which one of the following meets the condition required for the firm to be productively efficient? The firm is producing the quantity at which
options: average revenue equals average total cost.
average revenue equals marginal cost.
marginal cost equals average total cost.
marginal revenue equals marginal cost.

questions.questionText: Explain why, in long-run equilibrium, monopolistically competitive markets are neither productively nor allocatively efficient.
Explain how perfect competition should lead to outcomes which are both productively and allocatively efficient.

Figure 2 shows the equilibrium position, point E, of a profit-maximising firm in a monopolistically competitive industry. All other things being equal, which one of the following applies to the firm’s equilibrium at point E? The firm is
options: in short-run equilibrium, but not in long-run equilibrium.
making normal profit because AC = AR.
making supernormal profit because MC = MR.
productively efficient but not allocatively efficient.

questions.questionText: Figure 2 shows the production possibility frontier for an economy producing only two goods: chickens and cabbages. Which one of the following statements is true?
options: From the information given, it is impossible to determine whether point E is allocatively efficient
From the information given, it is impossible to determine whether point E is productively efficient
Point E is productively and allocatively efficient
Point E is productively efficient but allocatively inefficient

questions.questionText: Evaluate the view that a firm making low profits must be inefficiently managed.
Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 2) show that the UK parcels delivery market is displaying dynamic efficiency.
The diagram below shows the cost and revenue curves for a monopoly. At which one of the following levels of output would the firm be productively efficient?
options: OW
OX
OY
OZ

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows a production possibility boundary for an economy that produces goods and services. From the diagram it can be concluded that
options: point X is productively efficient and point Y is allocatively efficient.
point Y is productively efficient and point X is allocatively efficient.
points X and Y are allocatively efficient.
points X and Y are productively efficient.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows a firm’s average total cost curve (ATC), with the firm producing an output of OX. The firm’s productive efficiency will improve if the
options: ATC curve shifts upwards for any given level of output.
ATC curve shifts downwards for any given level of output.
firm increases its level of output.
firm reduces its level of output.
